subject: DatumHealth — model qualification, edge-case capture, and prompt intake
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Rao <asha@datumhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 1 Dec 2027 13:10:00 -0800
Subject: DatumHealth — model qualification, edge-case capture, and prompt intake

Hi Asha,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth for the evaluation phase.

Call recap (2 min):
- Primary goal: replace current on-prem NLU component with a hosted inference pipeline for triage + short-answer summarization across patient intake forms.
- Key constraints: PII redaction requirements (HIPAA), <200ms median latency target for short queries, and tight throughput spikes during mornings.
- Stakeholders: Product (you), Ops (procurement loop), Security (will want SOC2 evidence).

What Redwood will deliver for the model qualification:
1) Recommended model shortlist tuned for throughput/quality tradeoffs (we’ll include quantized variants).
2) A 2-week eval run against a representative prompt set you provide (we’ll run our bench and return token-level latency/cost and qualitative failure modes).
3) Simple redaction preprocessor patterns and a one-page redaction checklist for your security team.

What we need from DatumHealth:
- A seed prompt set: ~150–250 prompts (diverse: happy path, ambiguous phrasing, PII-heavy, low-context). CSV format is fine — see attached sample.
- A short taxonomy of edge-case tags you care about (e.g., DOB formats, non-English patient notes, OCR artifacts).
- Any internal SOPs for redaction/allowed PII retention windows.

Immediate ask / next steps:
1) Please upload your prompt CSV to the shared Drive folder linked below or attach it to a reply. We included a sample CSV attached (datum_prompts_sample.csv).
2) If security needs the redaction checklist earlier, flag us and we’ll prioritize.
3) Proposed timeline: receive prompts by 2027-12-07 → bench run 2027-12-08 to 2027-12-14 → share results and a short demo 2027-12-15.

Links: evaluation Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-datum-eval
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/76234/DH-2027-045

I’ll loop in Marissa who will own the bench run and Ben for pricing/commits if you need reserved capacity.

Thanks — Marcus

--
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments: datum_prompts_sample.csv (CSV, 45 rows)
From: Asha Rao <asha@datumhealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Product Team <product@datumhealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@datumhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Dec 2027 09:14:12 -0800
Subject: Re: DatumHealth — model qualification, edge-case capture, and prompt intake

Marcus — appreciate the clear recap. Two quick clarifications and I’ve uploaded the first batch to your Drive folder.

Clarifications:
- The latency target is an internal median of 200ms for responses under 32 tokens; 95th percentile can be up to 450ms during spikes.
- PII rules: we need to remove direct identifiers from downstream storage (name, SSN, MRN) but retain date ranges (month/year) for analytics. I’ve attached our brief SOP to the Drive folder as well.

What I uploaded:
- datum_prompts_initial_batch.csv (60 prompts — a mix of intake questions and OCR-transcribed notes).
- short SOP.pdf (internal redaction guidance).

We’ll follow up with a larger export next week. Can you confirm what format you prefer the edge-case taxonomy in? A simple CSV with columns (prompt_id, tag) works for us.

Also looping in Procurement — we’re tracking a pilot SOW and budget.

Thanks,
Asha

On Thu, Dec 2, 2027 at 09:14, Asha Rao <asha@datumhealth.com> wrote:
> Uploaded initial batch to Drive and included short SOP.
>
Attachments referenced: datum_prompts_initial_batch.csv
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Rao <asha@datumhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 3 Dec 2027 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DatumHealth — model qualification, edge-case capture, and prompt intake

Perfect — got the upload and SOP, thanks. A couple of follow-ups and what I’m attaching from our side.

1) Edge-case taxonomy: CSV works great. Please include columns: prompt_id, tag, severity (low/med/high), notes. Examples of tags: DOB-format, OCR-garbled, embedded-SN, non-English, multi-intent.

2) Model recommendations (shortlist) — high level:
- 'redwood-turbo-7b-fp16' (best latency/accuracy balance; we’ll run a quantized int8 variant if you need cost reduction).
- 'redwood-ggml-13b-q4' (higher quality on long-form but higher median latency).
- 'redwood-compact-3b' (edge-case heavy, low cost; good for initial triage).

Benchmarks: I kicked off a pre-run against a small synthetic slice so you can see the format. Results link: https://benchmarks.redwood.ai/datumhealth/2027-run-01 — it contains token-level latencies, cost estimates, and a short list of sample failures.

3) Redaction checklist: attached (redaction_checklist.pdf) — use it for an initial security review. It lists simple regex patterns we recommend and tests we run during the bench.

4) Attachments/Deliverables from Redwood:
- redaction_checklist.pdf (one-page)
- eval plan and expected metrics (I’ll drop the full run plan in the Drive folder by EOD)

Pricing / Reserved capacity note (Ben): Ben, based on the throughput targets (morning spike to ~60 RPS sustained for 20 minutes), do we have a quick back-of-envelope for a 30-day pilot?

Asha — once we have the full prompt set and taxonomy we’ll schedule the bench run and share a short recording of the worst failure modes so we can iterate on prompt engineering and redaction.

Thanks — Marcus

--
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Rao <asha@datumhealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 4 Dec 2027 16:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DatumHealth — model qualification, edge-case capture, and prompt intake

Hi Asha — quick note from the ops side so everyone has the schedule and deliverables.

What Redwood will need from DatumHealth to keep the 12/15 demo target: 
- Final prompt CSV (200 prompts recommended) uploaded to the Drive by EOD 2027-12-07.
- Edge-case taxonomy CSV (prompt_id, tag, severity) by 2027-12-08.
- Any PII retention exceptions documented in an email to security@redwood.ai by 2027-12-08; otherwise we’ll apply the default redaction_checklist.

Planned internal milestones:
- 12/08: Intake validation and pre-processing (marcus + marissa)
- 12/09–12/13: Bench runs and qualitative triage (marissa leads)
- 12/14: Internal results review and recording prep
- 12/15: Joint demo and findings review (30 min)

If Procurement needs a statement of work for the pilot, we attached a draft SOW to the Drive (datum_sow_v1.docx). Ben — please flag if any payment terms need to be adjusted for pilot work.

Asha — thanks again; we’ll review the initial batch today and ping with any clarifying prompt-level questions.

Best,
Marissa
